newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's HK mission accuses Japan rightists of threat.
newsitem.headline: China's HK mission accuses Japan rightists of threat.

text.p: A senior official from Beijing's de facto embassy in Hong Kong said on Tuesday it had received a threatening letter from a right-wing Japanese group amid a territorial dispute in the East China Sea.
Zhang Junsheng, a deputy director of the Xinhua News Agency's Hong Kong branch, said the Japanese government should guarantee the safety of Chinese people in Hong Kong, Taiwan and China.
"This (right-wing) organisation has not only threatened to kill and harm Chinese people, our Xinhua branch in Hong Kong has also received a threatening letter," Zhang told reporters.
"The Japanese government should take responsibility for controlling its own rightists...to guarantee the safety of Chinese people in Hong Kong, Taiwan and China," he said.

Tension over a group of potentially resource-rich islands, which China calls the Diaoyus and Japan calls the Senkakus, soared on Monday when Hong Kong and Taiwan activists pierced a Japanese maritime cordon and planted China and Taiwan flags.
Japan has claimed the islands since 1895 and refuses to admit that sovereignty is up for discussion while China has claimed them for centuries. Taipei also claims the islands, northeast of Taiwan.
Zhang said Tokyo should rein in right-wing extremists and "prevent them from poisoning good relations between China and Japan".
